title: Language tool manifest
description: The ONE declaration of what languages/<route>/tools.yaml may contain. Three readers: scripts/atlas.py (fails the contract on a manifest that does not conform), scripts/packprobe.py (parses each entry's kind from this grammar instead of guessing it), and languages/PACK-TOOLS-SPEC.md (whose skeleton is generated from this file). WHY IT EXISTS: the roles below are single-purpose fields that also held prose, so 49% of declared entries could not be evaluated by any instrument and the packs were unverifiable by construction. An entry now declares its KIND instead of leaving a probe to infer it from punctuation. BLIND SPOT: this file constrains the SHAPE of an entry, not its truth. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` and `go test` are the same shape; only the author knows which one PATH can find, which is why builtin:/lib:/concept: are written by hand and provenance.verify still carries the confirmation debt.

schema.description: Manifest format version. Bumped only by a change existing readers must handle: 2 renamed provenance.authored (a date) to provenance.since (a contract version), so a reader pinned to 1 is told rather than left to discover a missing field.

language.description: The pack's own basename, so a manifest copied into another pack fails the contract.

provenance.description: Where the entries came from and what is still unconfirmed. A manifest with no provenance reads as measured when it was recalled.

verify.description: Entries to confirm against the language's own documentation before a task relies on them. Empty means nothing is outstanding, never that nothing was ever doubted.

since.description: The CONTRACT VERSION this pack's entries were authored at, derived from the commit that introduced the manifest. A date records when somebody typed; a version records which tree the claim was true of, and only the second can be re-checked against anything.

authority.description: One role, one authority. Native toolchain first; MCP and AI layers are adapters, never authorities.

benchmark.description: How this language MEASURES a change in performance, which is not the same question as how it profiles one: a profiler says where the time went, a benchmark says whether the number moved and by how much. OPTIONAL in the schema so a reader pinned to format 2 is unaffected, and present in every pack so an absent role and an empty one are never confused.

profiles.description: What a task activates. An empty list is a real answer: this pack has nothing established for that task.

default_tools.description: Activated without being asked for. Capped by MAX_DEFAULT_TOOLS in atlas.py: a manifest that defaults to everything is not a bounded surface.

avoid_by_default.description: Habits this pack refuses. Policy words, not tool names — a manifest that names nothing to avoid has an unbounded surface.

blockers.description: What fails a change in this language. Named conditions, never tools.

notes.description: WHERE PROSE LIVES. Keyed by the role or profile it qualifies, so `carbon` can stay a probeable entry while 'experimental, built with bazel' stays readable. Never the place for an entry itself.

verification.description: OPTIONAL, and its absence is a real answer: a pack with no verification block claims only 'declared', which is what a manifest entry actually asserts. Every rung above that is a fact about a MACHINE, so claiming one requires naming the environment it was measured in. Rungs are declared in atlas.yaml/tool_claims and ordered — claiming one asserts every rung below it.

environment.description: Where it was measured. Required for any rung above 'declared'.

contract.description: The contract version it was measured at — never a date.

runner.description: HOW a non-command authority entry is actually invoked. A role may legitimately name a LIBRARY or a language BUILT-IN — `lib:hspec`, `builtin:ExUnit` — and neither is a shell command, so the gate that needs one cannot resolve. Measured at contract 2.22.0: 8 of 35 packs, and an A/B against a local model showed it INVENTS a plausible command in exactly that gap. This is where the pack says which command drives its library, so the gate resolves instead of the reader guessing. It may only be declared for a role whose authority entry is NOT already a command; a runner beside a command is a second declaration of one value.

entry.description: A DECLARED ENTRY. Its KIND is written by the author, not inferred by a reader: the command form is deliberately narrow (no parentheses, no slashes, no free words), because that is exactly how prose used to enter a field an instrument then had to skip. x-kinds below is the roster, and every reader — atlas.py, packprobe.py, PACK-TOOLS-SPEC.md — reads it from here.

command.means: the first word is a name PATH can resolve; `|` separates equivalent alternatives (`lldb|gdb`)

lib.means: a package or crate reachable only through its ecosystem, which PATH cannot answer for

builtin.means: a facility inside the language, runtime or editor; there is no binary to find

concept.means: a technique or a boundary rather than a tool

none.means: no established tool is known for this role; do not invent one

entryOrList.description: A list means a role genuinely needs several tools TOGETHER (`[ruff, bandit]`). It replaced `ruff+bandit`, where a probe read `+` as `or` and reported a role covered that was half covered.

url.description: Primary documentation. https only — a doc link that can be intercepted is not a source of authority.
